findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the clone lifecycle: who creates it, how each run refreshes it (fetch + reset to remote head) before folding, and the cleanup/reset behavior after a failed push.
evidence: 'its own .git, cloned from the tickets remote'
No statement of who provisions the clone, how it is refreshed between scheduled runs, or a cleanup path
findings.finding: The dedicated clone is shared state whose CREATE/REFRESH/RETIRE lifecycle is unspecified: the plan requires 'its own .git, cloned from the tickets remote' but never says who creates the clone, how it is kept fresh across runs (fetch/reset vs reclone), or whether/how stale clones are cleaned up.
findings.location: Approach — 'The sweep is designed to run in a real clone'
scenarios: Scheduled run N+1 reuses a clone left in a dirty/diverged state from a failed run N
Clone accumulates local commits after a rejected push and never resets
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step: each sweep run fetches and hard-resets the clone to the remote tip before enumerating, and resets local commits if the prior push was rejected.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the dedicated clone is created and how it inherits the REBAR signing key + engine identity (which command bootstraps it, where the key comes from), so the 'signs identically to in-place compaction' capability is verifiable rather than merely asserted.
evidence: Plan: 'its own .git, cloned from the tickets remote'
Plan: 'proving the env identity and signing key resolve outside the primary checkout'

Signing keys / engine identity are typically resolved via engine_env / config relative to the primary repo (see _bridge_probe's engine_env() usage in _cli/__init__.py); the plan names no mechanism by which the clone inherits REBAR signing identity
ABSENCE: Scope lists compact_sweep.py as 'enumerate, filter, fold via compact_cli, push once' but never states how/where the clone is created or how its signing env is populated
findings.finding: The plan asserts a new capability — compaction signing and env-identity resolving from a DEDICATED CLONE outside the primary checkout — but does not specify HOW the clone acquires the signing key / engine env, so the feasibility of the load-bearing 'signs identically' claim cannot be verified from the plan text.
findings.location: Approach (dedicated-clone bullet) + Testing ('Signing from a fresh clone') + AC line 5
scenarios: A scheduled sweep runs in a clone with no signing key configured and either fails to sign or signs with a wrong/absent identity, producing events the merge-gate rebar verify-authorship rejects
The clone's git author (user.name via _git_author) differs from the primary checkout, changing the authorship ledger
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach/Scope, name the clone-bootstrap step (e.g. `git clone <tickets-remote>` + which env/config keys carry the signing identity into the clone), and if signing-in-a-clone has not been exercised before, gate the full plan behind a short SPIKE that runs one compaction in a fresh clone and diffs its authorship ledger + signatures against an in-place run.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion covering the rejected-push failure path (clone commits intact, failure reported, neither store corrupted).
evidence: Testing: 'Failure path: a sweep whose push is rejected leaves the clone's local commits intact and reports the failure rather than corrupting either store.'
Acceptance Criteria list has no push-rejection item
findings.finding: The Testing section lists a 'Failure path' (rejected push leaves clone commits intact and reports failure) but there is no corresponding Acceptance Criterion, so this described deliverable has no covering criterion.
scenarios: Reviewer signing off checks ACs only and never verifies the failure-handling behavior
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: '[ ] A sweep whose push is rejected reports the failure and leaves the clone's commits intact — a test asserts non-corrupting behavior and a failure exit/summary.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify where a failed scheduled sweep surfaces (log/exit code/alert) and whether it retries on transient push rejection, so operators can detect a persistently failing compactor.
evidence: 'reports the failure rather than corrupting either store' — reporting target for an unattended job is unspecified
No metric/log/alert for a silently-failing scheduled compactor
findings.finding: As an unattended scheduled write operation, the sweep's failure handling is under-specified beyond 'reports the failure': there is no stated retry/backoff, no alerting/observability so an operator learns the scheduled sweep is failing, and no defined behavior when a push is repeatedly rejected.
scenarios: Scheduled sweep starts failing every run; nobody notices; store event logs grow unbounded again — the exact problem this ticket fixes
findings.suggested_fix: State that a rejected push retries after a fresh fetch/reset up to a small bound, and a persistent failure exits non-zero / emits a log the scheduler surfaces.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the sweep suppresses compact_cli's per-ticket push (e.g. invoke each fold with --skip-sync/--no-commit and do a single batched commit+push like compact_all's _commit_backfill) so the 'exactly one push' in AC-1 is achievable.
evidence: Plan: 'by calling the existing compact_cli ... per ticket, then pushes once through the normal push path (rebar._store.push)'
compact.py:136-139 — compact_cli calls push.push_after_commit(tracker) after each successful fold unless no_commit or skip_sync
compact.py:132-135 comment: compact-all batches one commit + push itself by passing --skip-sync per ticket (bug prone-octet-cheek)
findings.finding: The plan's 'push once' mechanism contradicts the existing compact_cli push behavior it drives over. compact_cli pushes per-ticket best-effort (compact.py:136-139) UNLESS --skip-sync or --no-commit is passed; the plan says the sweep folds 'via compact_cli per ticket, then pushes once' and AC-1 asserts 'exactly one push', but never specifies how the N per-ticket pushes are suppressed. As written the sweep would push once per over-threshold ticket, violating its own acceptance criterion.
findings.location: Approach bullet 1 ('pushes once through the normal push path') and AC-1 ('pushes once ... exactly one push')
scenarios: A sweep over 50 over-threshold tickets issues 50 pushes instead of one, contending on the remote and failing AC-1's 'exactly one push' assertion
findings.suggested_fix: State that each per-ticket fold is invoked with --skip-sync (and/or --no-commit) so compact_cli does not push, and the sweep stages+commits the batch once and calls push.push_after_commit exactly once at the end — mirroring compact_all_cli / _commit_backfill (compact.py:190-210).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify why a new `compact-sweep` module/verb is needed instead of extending the existing `compact-all` driver (`compact_all_cli`, compact.py:213) — which already enumerates ticket dirs, folds via `compact_cli --skip-sync --no-commit`, and pushes once — with a threshold-based filter; or reframe the sweep as the dedicated-clone/scheduled invocation of compact-all.
evidence: `compact_all_cli` exists at src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:213 and is registered as `compact-all` (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:116 `_COMPACT = frozenset({"compact", "compact-all"})`, dispatch at :304).

compact-all is already the exact 'driver over compact_txn' the plan describes: it loops `compact_cli([tid, '--threshold=0', '--skip-sync', '--no-commit'])` (compact.py:252) then `_commit_backfill` does one `git add -A` + commit + `push.push_after_commit` (compact.py:190-210).

The only real difference is the enumeration filter: compact-all uses `_scan_snapshot_state` = tickets lacking a `-SNAPSHOT.json` (compact.py:144), while the sweep wants tickets whose event count exceeds `compact.threshold` — a filter-predicate change, not a new module.
compact-all already carries `--dry-run` / `--limit` / `--no-commit` scaffolding a sweep would want; the plan's Scope re-invents this.
The verbatim plan references `compact_cli`, `compact_txn`, `_retire_folded_sources`, `_sync_before_compact` but never `compact_all_cli` / `compact-all` — the duplication is unacknowledged.
findings.finding: The plan proposes a new module and verb (`compact_sweep.py` / `rebar compact-sweep`) that duplicates the existing bulk-compaction driver `compact_all_cli` (`rebar compact-all`), which already enumerates ticket dirs, folds each via `compact_cli` with `--skip-sync --no-commit`, and commits+pushes exactly once; the plan never mentions `compact-all` or why extending it (changing its filter from 'lacks a SNAPSHOT' to 'over `compact.threshold`') is insufficient.
findings.location: Scope: `src/rebar/_commands/compact_sweep.py` — new; and Approach bullet 1 ('A maintenance verb `rebar compact-sweep` ... calling the existing `compact_cli` ... then pushes once ... No new fold engine: the verb is a driver over compact_txn')
scenarios: Two bulk-compaction verbs (`compact-all`, `compact-sweep`) now coexist with near-identical drivers, diverging over time (e.g. one gains a bug-fix or flag the other lacks).
The dedicated-clone execution model the plan actually cares about is orthogonal to which verb runs — `compact-all` run from a clone would achieve the same isolation.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold the threshold-filter enumeration into `compact-all` (e.g. an `--over-threshold` / `--min-events=N` selection mode beside the existing lacks-SNAPSHOT scan) and make 'the sweep' the scheduled dedicated-clone invocation of that verb, rather than a second driver module. If a distinct verb is genuinely warranted, state explicitly what compact-all cannot express and why the driver cannot be shared.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Address compact_all_cli (compact.py:213) as the closest existing driver: state why compact-sweep is a distinct verb rather than a generalization of compact-all's filter (over-threshold + re-fold-on-regrowth), and reuse its enumerate/_commit_backfill batching instead of re-implementing it.
evidence: compact.py:213 compact_all_cli — existing 'enumerate, filter, fold per ticket, commit+push once' driver
compact.py:144-163 _scan_snapshot_state enumerates ticket dirs and partitions by SNAPSHOT presence
compact.py:190-210 _commit_backfill — the single-commit+push batching the sweep also needs
Plan Scope lists a brand-new module with the same enumerate/filter/fold/push-once shape and no reference to compact-all
findings.finding: The plan proposes a wholly new verb/module (compact_sweep.py) without acknowledging compact_all_cli (compact.py:213), which is a structurally near-identical existing driver: it enumerates ticket dirs, filters, folds each via the txn engine with --skip-sync, and commits+pushes ONCE via _commit_backfill. The sweep differs only in the FILTER (event-count-over-threshold vs. lacking-a-SNAPSHOT) and in re-folding already-snapshotted tickets whose logs regrew. The plan neither cites this closest prior art nor gives a positive reason a new verb beats generalizing compact-all's filter, which weakens codebase-alignment and duplicates enumerate/batch/push logic.
findings.location: Approach bullet 1 and Scope ('src/rebar/_commands/compact_sweep.py — new: the sweep driver')
scenarios: Implementer re-writes enumerate + batch-commit + push logic that compact_all already contains, risking drift between the two drivers' commit/push semantics

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the 'add vs rename+add merges cleanly' claim against git's actual merge semantics (rename-detection thresholds, add/add on identical SNAPSHOT paths, delete/modify degradation) with a concrete merge fixture, rather than asserting it.
evidence: Plan: 'it adds one -SNAPSHOT.json file and renames folded sources to *.retired ... Git merges an add against a rename+add without conflict.'

Retrieved: kernel.org git-merge-tree(1) — three-way merge uses 'rename detection' and 'proper directory/file conflict handling', confirming rename handling is a heuristic feature rather than a guarantee
Every convergence AC (double-snapshot, mixed-version, concurrent-tail) inherits correctness from this single unverified claim

compact_txn._retire_folded_sources renames sources to *.retired and the caller writes a timestamp+uuid-named SNAPSHOT (src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:232-253) — the double-snapshot case yields two different SNAPSHOT files that must BOTH survive the merge for 'no lost events' to hold
findings.finding: The convergence argument's keystone — 'Git merges an add against a rename+add without conflict' — is a load-bearing capability assertion resolved only by internal reasoning, not against git's documented merge semantics. Git rename detection is a heuristic gated by similarity thresholds and merge.renameLimit, and the double-snapshot race (two sweeps folding the SAME ticket) produces two SNAPSHOT files whose names embed distinct timestamp/uuid — but if any code path can produce the SAME snapshot path, that is an add/add conflict, not a clean merge. The plan should verify this claim (e.g. via git-merge-tree behavior / a rename+add merge fixture) rather than assert it.
findings.location: Approach / 'This works because a compaction's output is merge-clean'
scenarios: Two sweeps fold the same over-threshold ticket concurrently and push; the merge must retain both -SNAPSHOT files and both rename-to-retired without treating either as a delete/modify or add/add conflict
A rename+add where git's -M similarity heuristic fails to detect the rename, degrading it to delete+add and risking a delete/modify conflict against the other side's snapshot content

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Frame the scheduled-sweep trigger choice against the established `git maintenance` / `git gc --auto` background-housekeeping pattern, naming what rebar borrows (out-of-interactive-path scheduling) and what is genuinely novel (dedicated-clone lock isolation).
evidence: Plan: 'a SCHEDULED sweep (documented, with the cadence recorded in docs/concurrency.md), chosen over per-close detached workers because it is one amortized pass instead of one process per close'

Retrieved prior art: git-scm.com/docs/git-maintenance — 'updates the background scheduler to run git maintenance run --scheduled on an hourly basis' — the established pattern for scheduled background store housekeeping
The rebar-specific novelty is the dedicated-clone isolation to avoid the shared store write lock; this is the part warranting an anti-repackaging justification
findings.finding: The plan chooses a scheduled out-of-band compactor over per-close detached workers on operational grounds but does not consider the canonical prior art for this pattern — git's own `git maintenance` / `git gc --auto` (scheduled background store housekeeping run out of the interactive path). The novelty (running in a dedicated clone, reconciled via push) may be justified, but the justification should be framed against that established approach rather than presented as first principles.
scenarios: Reviewer or future maintainer asks why not model the trigger on git's own maintenance scheduler idioms (systemd timer / launchd / CI cron) already documented and battle-tested
